title: Finish the type check
hints: Each broken branch needs a check before it answers, like the `a == b` check in the first branch.
For `cmplt` the result does not depend on `a`: comparing two `i32` values gives a `bool`.
`return "bool" if a == b else "rejected"` for `cmplt`, and `return "i32" if a == "i32" and b == "i32" else "rejected"` for the last three.
prompt:
result_dtype(op, a, b) is given an op and the dtypes of its two operands, each "i32" or "bool". It returns the dtype of the result, or "rejected" when the op does not accept those operands.

The branch for add, mul, max and xor is right. Two branches are too trusting. cmplt needs both operands to have the same dtype, and its result is always "bool". div, mod and shl need both operands to be "i32".

answer.explain: Each op has one rule. `add`, `mul`, `max` and `xor` need two operands of the same dtype and give that dtype back. `cmplt` needs the same, but its answer is a yes or a no, so the result is always `bool`. `div`, `mod` and `shl` only make sense on numbers, so both operands must be `i32`. Anything else is refused before the program runs.
